pyq-t24-ex3.statement: A0 = 10⁵, fp = 10 Hz, otherwise ideal, non-inverting with closed-loop gain 100. Find the frequency where |Aβ| = 1, and the phase margin.

inShort.concept: β = 1/100, so βA0 = 1000: the loop gain crosses 1 three decades above the pole. One pole can never take more than 90°.

steps.title: PM

pyq-t24-ex4.title: Past tutorial: closed-loop gain at ω1 for PM 30°, 60°, 90°
pyq-t24-ex4.statement: Find the closed-loop gain at ω1 (where |Aβ| = 1) relative to the low-frequency gain, for phase margins of 30°, 60° and 90°.

inShort.concept: Same as Lec 16: at ω1 the denominator is |1 + e^{−j(180°−PM)}| = 2 sin(PM/2).

steps.title: PM 30°: peaks
PM 60°: exactly no peak
PM 90°: the usual −3 dB point

hints: With θ = PM − 180°, that is 2 sin(PM/2).

pyq-t24-ex56.title: Past tutorial: dominant-pole compensation for closed-loop gains down to 20 dB
pyq-t24-ex56.statement: A multipole amplifier: first pole 1 MHz, DC gain 100 dB, second pole 10 MHz. (Ex 5) Where must a new dominant pole go so it is stable for closed-loop gains as low as 20 dB? (Ex 6) Instead, lower the first pole (second pole unchanged): to what frequency, and by what factor must that node’s capacitance grow?

inShort.concept: Gain 20 dB → β = 0.1 → βA0 = 10⁴. Make the loop gain fall at −20 dB/dec from the new pole to 0 dB exactly where the next pole sits (≈45° PM, Sedra’s rule used in this tutorial).

steps.title: Ex 5: from βA0 = 10⁴ down to 1 at 1 MHz takes four decades
Ex 6: now the crossover is the second pole, 10 MHz
The pole is 1/(RC): C grows by the same factor

hints: Unity loop gain at the next pole.

bank-r10-1.title: Razavi 10.1: the largest A0 for 60° phase margin
bank-r10-1.statement: An amplifier with DC gain A0 has two poles, at 10 MHz and 500 MHz, and is used in unity-gain feedback. What A0 gives a phase margin of exactly 60°?

steps.title: PM = 60° means the loop phase at ωgx is −120°
The first pole gives almost 90°, so the second must give about 30°: fgx a bit above 500·tan 30° = 289 MHz. Exactly:
Make |βA| = 1 there
Only about 36: two poles 50× apart leave very little room for gain at 60°

bank-lec16.title: Lec 16: how much the closed loop peaks at PM = 5°, 45°, 60°
bank-lec16.statement: Your Lec 16 notes compute |Af(ωgx)| for three phase margins. Using |βA(ωgx)| = 1, find |Af(ωgx)| as a multiple of 1/β for PM = 5°, 45° and 60°.

steps.title: PM = 60° → ∠βA = −120°: exactly no peak
Shortcut for all three: 1/(2 sin(PM/2))

hints: Write βA as cos θ + j sin θ with θ = PM − 180°.

bank-ex10-6.title: Razavi Ex 10.6: first estimate of CC for 45°
bank-ex10-6.statement: A Miller-compensated two-stage op amp has first-stage gm1 = 1 mS, second-stage gm9 = 5 mS and CL = 2 pF. Estimate CC for a 45° phase margin in unity-gain feedback: (a) ignoring the second pole’s effect on the magnitude, (b) including it.

steps.title: After compensation: p1 ≈ 1/(gm9RLCCRS), p2 ≈ gm9/CL. For 45° the loop gain must reach 1 right at p2
Loop gain above p1 falls as gm1/(ωCC); set it to 1 at ω = gm9/CL
At p2 the second pole already cuts |βA| by √2
A starting point: real designs use a larger CC (60°) and a smaller one if β < 1

hints: 45°: put the gain crossover on the second pole.
flags: Numbers chosen by the app (the book states this example with symbols only).

bank-ps2-p2.title: PS2 P2: phase margin at gain 1 and at gain 5
bank-ps2-p2.statement: An op amp has A0 = 2000 and poles at 50 kHz and 50 MHz. Find ωgx and the phase margin (a) as a unity-gain buffer and (b) with β = 0.2. (c) How much does the buffer peak at ωgx?

steps.title: (a) βA0 = 2000; solve (1 + f²/fp1²)(1 + f²/fp2²) = 2000²
PM = 180° − atan(fgx/fp1) − atan(fgx/fp2)
(b) β = 0.2: the gain curve drops by 14 dB, ωgx moves left, the phase there is kinder
(c) 1/(2 sin(PM/2)) for the buffer

hints: βA0·fp1 = 100 MHz: that is above fp2!

bank-ps2-p3.title: PS2 P3: compensate the Lec 17 three-pole amplifier
bank-ps2-p3.statement: The Lec 17 amplifier: A0 = 100 dB, poles at 1 kHz, 1 MHz and 10 MHz, used for a closed-loop gain of 10 (β = 0.1). (a) The phase margin as built. (b) Keeping the 1 MHz and 10 MHz poles, where must the first pole go for PM = 45°? (c) By what factor must its capacitor grow?

steps.title: (a) βA0 = 10⁴ (80 dB above the 1/β line): find ωgx numerically, then the phase: almost nothing left
(b) The two high poles may use only 90° − 45° = 45° at the new ωgx
−20 dB/dec from βA0 = 10⁴ down to 0 dB at ωgx
(c) The pole is 1/(RC): C grows by the same factor

hints: Work on the loop gain βA, not A.
Where do the 1 MHz and 10 MHz poles give 45° together?
The new ωgx is 844 kHz, so the first pole goes to about 84 Hz.

bank-ps2-p4.title: PS2 P4: add a second stage to your exam OTA and compensate it
bank-ps2-p4.statement: Your exam OTA (Gm1 = 0.8 mS, R1 = 111 kΩ, C1 = 0.1 pF, ISS = 120 µA) drives a PMOS CS stage M6 (Gm2 = 4 mS, R2 = 20 kΩ) biased by I7 = 500 µA, loaded by CL = 4 pF. With Rz = 1/Gm2: (a) CC for PM = 60° (β = 1, ωp2 ≈ Gm2/CL); (b) the GBW; (c) the dominant pole P1′ ≈ 1/(R1A2CC); (d) Rz; (e) the slew rate.

steps.title: (a) ωp2 = ωu·tan 60°: Gm2/CL = (Gm1/CC)·1.732
(b) GBW = Gm1/(2πCC)
(c) A2 = Gm2R2 = 80; node 1 sees CC(1 + A2)
(d) Rz = 1/Gm2 moves the RHP zero to infinity
(e) ISS/CC vs (I7 − ISS)/CL: the smaller wins

bank-r10-2.title: Razavi 10.2: two equal poles, 60° margin, gain 1 and gain 4
bank-r10-2.statement: An amplifier has two poles at the same frequency ωp. What is the largest DC gain A0 for a 60° phase margin when the closed-loop gain is (a) 1 and (b) 4?

steps.title: Each pole must give 60° at ωgx (together 120°)
There |βA| = βA0/(1 + 3) = 1
(b) β = 1/4: weaker feedback allows four times the gain

hints: Equal poles share the phase equally.
Each gives 60° at ωgx: ωgx = ωp·tan 60°.

pyq-m25-q2.title: 2025 mid-sem Q2: design a Miller-compensated two-stage op amp
pyq-m25-q2.statement: Design the two-stage op amp (find every W/L, I and Cc): DC gain 60 dB, GBW = 50 MHz, PM ≥ 60°, SR = 50 V/µs, ICMR(+) = 1.6 V, ICMR(−) = 0.9 V, CL = 5 pF. Use the minimum Cc for 60°. The mirror M3–M4 is perfect when sizing M7; M5 and M6 are the same size. µnCox = 300 µA/V², Vth1(max) = 0.59 V, Vth1(min) = 0.47 V, µpCox = 60 µA/V², |Vth3(max)| = 0.51 V, VDD = 1.8 V.

inShort.concept: The standard seven-step Miller design: Cc from the phase margin, the tail current from the slew rate, gm1 from the GBW, then each W/L from one spec (ICMR+ sizes the mirror, ICMR− sizes the tail, the RHP zero sizes the output device).

steps.title: ① Cc for 60° with the zero at 10·GB: Cc ≥ 0.22 CL
② Slew rate sets the tail current (M5 = M6 so I = I5)
③ GBW sets gm1; square law gives (W/L)1,2 at ID1 = I5/2
④ ICMR(+): M1 at its edge against M3’s diode drop (worst-case thresholds)
⑤ ICMR(−): what is left for the tail after VGS1
⑥ RHP zero at 10·GB → gm7 = 10gm1; perfect mirror → |Vov7| = |Vov3|
⑦ M8 mirrors M5 and must carry I7

hints: Go in the fixed order: Cc, I5, gm1, (W/L)1, (W/L)3, (W/L)5, (W/L)7, (W/L)8.
Cc ≥ 0.22CL is the 60° rule when the RHP zero sits at 10·GB.
ICMR(+) uses the smallest Vth1 and the largest |Vth3|; ICMR(−) uses the largest Vth1.
gm7 ≥ 10gm1 puts the RHP zero at 10·GB.
flags: The 60 dB DC-gain spec is not used in the key’s sizing (the gain comes out well above it).

bank-r10-3.title: Razavi 10.3: A0 = 1000 with two close poles
bank-r10-3.statement: An amplifier has A0 = 1000 and poles at ωp1 = 1 MHz and ωp2. In unity-gain feedback, what is the phase margin if (a) ωp2 = 2ωp1 and (b) ωp2 = 4ωp1? (Frequencies in Hz here.)

steps.title: |βA| = 1: (1 + f²/fp1²)(1 + f²/fp2²) = 10⁶, a quadratic in f²
(a) Both poles are far below ωgx: each gives nearly 90°
(b) Moving fp2 up helps only a little
Almost oscillating: with this much gain the second pole must be far above A0·fp1 = 1 GHz

bank-r10-4.title: Razavi 10.4: 50% peaking → what phase margin?
bank-r10-4.statement: A unity-gain feedback amplifier peaks by 50% near the gain crossover. What is its phase margin?

steps.title: At ωgx: |βA| = 1 and ∠βA = PM − 180°, so |1 + βA| = 2 sin(PM/2)
Set it equal to 1.5/β
Check with Lec 16: 45° gives 1.3×, 60° gives 1.0×, so 1.5× must be below 45°

pyq-m23-q3.title: 2023 mid-sem Q3: design a high-swing PMOS-input telescopic
pyq-m23-q3.statement: All PMOS about the same size, all NMOS the same size. SR = 5 V/µs into 10 pF; Vout,max = 1.28 V, Vout,min = 0.3 V, VDD = 2 V. µnCox = 100 µA/V², µpCox = 50 µA/V², Vthn = 0.3 V, Vthp = −0.4 V, λn = 0.1, λp = 0.2 V⁻¹ (L = 1 µm). Find all sizes, Vb1,min, Vb2,max, Vb3 and the gain.

inShort.concept: Slew rate fixes ISS. The swing limits fix the overdrives: the floor is two NMOS overdrives (high-swing mirror), the ceiling is VDD minus three PMOS overdrives (M9 carries twice the current, so its overdrive is √2 larger). Square law gives W/L; bias voltages put each device at its edge.
formulas: I_{SS} = SR\cdot C_L,\quad V_{out,min} = V_{ov8} + V_{ov6}

steps.title: Slew rate: ISS = SR·CL = 50 µA, 25 µA per side
Floor 0.3 V = two NMOS overdrives
Ceiling: 2 − 1.28 = 0.72 V shared by M9 (√2·|Vov|) and M2, M4
Vb1,min: M7 at its edge under cascode M5
Vb2,max: M2 at its edge (its drain is M4’s source)
Vb3 biases the tail M9 (50 µA)
Gain: gm2 (Rup ‖ Rdown)

hints: The high-swing NMOS mirror leaves only two overdrives at the bottom.
M9 carries 2ID: same W/L means √2 times the overdrive.
Each bias voltage puts one device exactly at its edge.
flags: The key prints (W/L)1–4 = 22.67 (it rounds |Vov| to 0.21) and (W/L)9 = 22.22. Both are inside ±3%.

bank-t2q2.title: Tutorial 2 Q2: telescopic with a diode-connected cascode mirror
bank-t2q2.statement: Set A (Razavi 0.5 µm): µnCox = 134.28 µA/V², µpCox = 38.36 µA/V², λn = 0.1 V⁻¹, λp = 0.2 V⁻¹ (L = 0.5 µm), Vthn = 0.7 V, |Vthp| = 0.8 V, VDD = 3 V, γ = 0. The single-ended telescopic (Fig. 9.9 style): (W/L)1–4 = 100/0.5, ISS = 1 mA, Vb = 1.4 V; M5–M8 identical, L = 0.5 µm. (a) Minimum PMOS width for M3 to stay saturated. (b) Maximum output swing. (c) Open-loop gain.

unknowns.label: (b) Highest output (M2 gate on the output)

steps.title: Two PMOS diodes stack from VDD: M3’s drain sits at VDD − 2|VGS,p|. Fence: VD3 ≥ Vb − Vthn
Smallest W/L that carries 0.5 mA at that overdrive
Floor: M4 fence, Vout ≥ Vb − Vth4
Ceiling from the stacks is VDD − |Vthp| − 2|Vov,p| = 1.50 V, but M2’s gate is on Vout: M2 leaves saturation above Vb − VGS4 + Vth2
Gain: gm1 (Rdown ‖ Rup), both ≈ gm·rO²

hints: Where does M3’s drain sit? Count the diode drops from VDD.
M3 saturated needs VD3 ≥ Vb − Vthn.
flags: Disagreement (inventory flag 8): your preliminary range was 0.70–1.50 V. That is right for the cascode stacks alone, but in Fig. 9.9 M2’s gate is tied to Vout, so the real top is 1.21 V (the Vth − Vov window of Ex 9.5).

bank-lab3.title: Lab 3: CS versus cascode gain, bandwidth and GBW
bank-lab3.statement: ID = 20 µA, V* = 200 mV, CL = 1 pF, ideal current-source loads. Example chart reading: VA = 5 V (rO = VA/ID). Find gm, the CS gain gm·rO, the cascode gain ≈ (gm·rO)², the CS bandwidth and the GBW of both.

steps.title: gm from V*
CS with an ideal load: intrinsic gain 2VA/V*
Cascode (cascoded load too): about the square
CS pole at the output
GBW = gm/(2πCL) for both: the cascode trades bandwidth for gain one-for-one

flags: This uses an example chart reading so you can practise the method; in the lab you read the value from your own V* chart.

bank-ps1p10.title: PS1 P10: capstone, design for settling and swing
bank-ps1p10.statement: Set B: µnCox = 200 µA/V², µpCox = 100 µA/V², λn = 0.05 V⁻¹, λp = 0.1 V⁻¹, Vthn = 0.4 V, |Vthp| = 0.5 V, VDD = 1.8 V. Design a fully differential op amp: gain ≥ 500, differential swing ≥ 1.2 Vpp, CL = 2 pF, settle to 0.1% in 20 ns in unity-gain feedback, input CM = output CM. (a) Topology. (b) Required gm1,2. (c) Overdrive of the four swing-critical devices. (d) Currents, gain, power.

steps.title: (a) Unity-gain feedback with input CM = output CM: the telescopic is trapped in a Vth − Vov window. Fold
(b) β = 1: τ = 1/ωu; 0.1% in 20 ns needs 6.91τ ≤ 20 ns
(c) Each output swings 0.6 V; four overdrives share 1.8 − 0.6 = 1.2 V

hints: Which topology can have input CM = output CM in unity gain?
gm = ωu·CL; four overdrives from the swing.
